result.title: DriftWAM: Faster World-Action Models via Action-Aware Video Drifting
result.summary: World-action models (WAMs) unify future video prediction and action generation for robotic control, but their reliance on iterative denoising incurs substantial inference costs. Distilling these models into few-step generators offers a promising route to efficient deployment, yet maintaining task performance under aggressive step reduction remains challenging. Existing methods rely on point-wise trajectory consistency distillation, which pursues high visual fidelity while leaving downstream action information unexploited in optimizing video generation, and also lacks explicit distribution-level alignment. To address this, we propose DriftWAM, a few-step WAM distillation framework that incorporates the actions induced by predicted videos into video learning. Specifically, DriftWAM integrates action-aware video drifting, which performs video distribution matching through a joint visual--action similarity kernel to steer sample evolution under the guidance of these induced actions, with action-guided video regularization, which leverages the compatible teacher--student matches identified by the joint kernel to backpropagate action-level gradients directly into the video generator. Evaluations on the RoboTwin 2.0 and LIBERO benchmarks, as well as in real-world robotic manipulation tasks, show that DriftWAM consistently outperforms prior consistency distillation methods across few-step settings at the same inference speed.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 DriftWAM，一种面向世界-动作模型（WAM）的少步蒸馏框架：用联合视觉-动作相似度核做视频分布匹配的「action-aware video drifting」，并借动作级梯度回传正则化视频生成器，在 RoboTwin 2.0、LIBERO 与真机操作上验证少步设置下的效果。
AI.relevance_reason: 把下游动作信号嵌入生成分布的匹配核、而非只追求逐点轨迹一致，可能为 LVR 中「压缩潜在推理步数仍保住答案正确性」的轨迹蒸馏与任务级贡献分配提供可核查线索；但该工作属机器人世界模型，迁移到视觉推理状态需进一步判断。
